findings.highlight: My happy mind
findings.evidenceJa: 舞い上がっていた意識
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s elated, soaring consciousness
findings.explanation: Happy mind is unnatural English and flattens the sense that Shirou’s consciousness had been carried aloft before freezing instantly.

findings.highlight: Her hand holds me tightly
findings.evidenceJa: 重ねた指が強く握られる
findings.governingReading: The fingers Shirou and Saber had laid together are gripped hard.
findings.explanation: The English changes joined fingers into Saber’s whole hand holding Shirou and weakens continuity with the preceding handholding.

findings.highlight: inconcealable desperation
findings.evidenceJa: 覆しようのない絶望
findings.governingReading: despair that cannot be overturned
findings.explanation: Inconcealable concerns hiding emotion; the source says the despairing outcome cannot be reversed. Desperation also shifts 絶望 from absence of hope to urgent effort.

findings.highlight: even Caster herself without any difficulty
findings.evidenceJa: 逃げようとするキャスターすら、事も無げに始末した
findings.governingReading: effortlessly disposed even of Caster as she tried to escape
findings.explanation: The English omits that Caster was attempting to flee when the golden Servant finished her.

findings.highlight: At a distance with which we could start fighting if we wanted to face a “death” greater than Berserker.
findings.evidenceJa: その気になればすぐにでも斬り合いを始められる距離
findings.governingReading: At a distance close enough that a swordfight could begin the instant either side chose
findings.explanation: The English attaches the Berserker comparison to wanting to fight and produces a malformed spatial sentence, obscuring how immediately violence can begin.

findings.highlight: as if evaluating a work of art
findings.evidenceJa: 気に入った美術品の品定めをするように
findings.governingReading: as though appraising a work of art that had caught his fancy
findings.explanation: The English omits that Saber is already an object he likes, sharpening the proprietary gaze behind his appraisal.

findings.highlight: She must have prepared herself.
findings.evidenceJa: 覚悟を決めたのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps Saber has steeled her resolve.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s question about Saber’s changed presence into certainty and weakens 覚悟 to generic preparation.

findings.highlight: Please retreat from here in that time.
findings.evidenceJa: その隙に、貴方だけは離脱してください
findings.governingReading: Use the opening created by the blocked first strike to escape by yourself.
findings.explanation: In that time turns a tactical opening into generic duration and softens Saber’s insistence that Shirou alone withdraw.

findings.highlight: The chance of success of retreating from a guy like this is low.
findings.evidenceJa: あまりにも成功率が低すぎる
findings.governingReading: The chance of escaping is far, far too low.
findings.explanation: Low removes the emphatic excess expressed by both あまりにも and 低すぎる.

findings.highlight: For some reason, I know
findings.evidenceJa: 確証もなく思った
findings.governingReading: He thinks it without any firm evidence.
findings.explanation: The English reverses explicit lack of certainty into knowledge.

findings.highlight: It should be able to shelter you even against him
findings.evidenceJa: あいつなら、アレが相手でもおまえを匿ってくれる筈
findings.governingReading: Kotomine should shelter Saber even from that enemy.
findings.explanation: The English makes the church building the sheltering actor, erasing Shirou’s reliance on Kotomine as a person.

findings.highlight: a big hammer
findings.evidenceJa: 巨大な鉄槌
findings.governingReading: a gigantic iron hammer that sends Shirou flying like trash before he lands on the ground
findings.explanation: Big omits both iron and the exceptional scale; the surrounding English also changes landing after flight into being smashed “across” the ground.

findings.highlight: I shall let you live until the Holy Grail appears.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を呼ぶまでは生かしておいてやろう
findings.governingReading: He will keep Shirou alive until the Grail is summoned.
findings.explanation: Appears removes the deliberate ritual act of calling forth the Grail.

findings.highlight: ways to let a Servant stay in this world
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを存命させる方法
findings.governingReading: ways to keep a Servant alive
findings.explanation: Stay in this world substitutes location for survival and weakens the threat that Shirou is dispensable to Saber’s continued life.

findings.highlight: I will kill you if you annoy me.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以上さえずるのなら殺すぞ
findings.governingReading: If Shirou chirps or prattles any further, he will be killed.
findings.explanation: Annoy me replaces a concrete condition—continuing to speak—with the enemy’s subjective irritation.

findings.highlight: That kills my mind.
findings.evidenceJa: それで、心が死んだ
findings.governingReading: At that, Shirou’s heart or spirit dies.
findings.explanation: Kills my mind is nonidiomatic and can suggest cognitive destruction rather than fear crushing his will to resist.

findings.highlight: he will do so without hesitation
findings.evidenceJa: なんの苦労もかけずに実行する
findings.governingReading: he will carry out the killing without the slightest effort or trouble
findings.explanation: Without hesitation changes ease of execution into decisiveness.

findings.highlight: after being told that
findings.evidenceJa: そんな事実を見せつけられて
findings.governingReading: after having that fact forcibly demonstrated before him
findings.explanation: Told reduces bodily proof of overwhelming power to verbal information.

findings.highlight: you are not willing to come to me
findings.evidenceJa: 我に下る気はない
findings.governingReading: you still have no intention of submitting to me
findings.explanation: Come to me replaces political and personal submission with physical approach.

findings.highlight: It should be a woman’s joy to be held down and be violated.
findings.evidenceJa: 主の前に頭を垂れ、仕え、尽くすが女の幸せ
findings.governingReading: He claims a woman’s happiness is to bow before her lord, serve him, and devote herself.
findings.explanation: The active English contains an abandoned variant inventing sexual restraint and violation before a second translation of the same sentence.

findings.highlight: It is not like you are a virgin.
findings.evidenceJa: 物も判らぬ小娘でもあるまいし
findings.governingReading: You are surely not some little girl who understands nothing.
findings.explanation: An active abandoned variant turns lack of worldly understanding into sexual experience.

findings.highlight: I do not want to live with you.
findings.evidenceJa: まかり間違ってもありえません
findings.governingReading: Living with him is absolutely impossible under any conceivable circumstances.
findings.explanation: Do not want reduces Saber’s categorical impossibility to personal preference.

findings.highlight: Yes, there must be at least one that will not obey me…!
findings.evidenceJa: ああ、この世に一つ程度は、我に従わぬモノがいなければな
findings.governingReading: At least one thing in this world must exist that refuses to obey him.
findings.explanation: The English leaves Archer’s quotation unclosed across the page boundary, making subsequent narration appear to remain inside his speech.

findings.highlight: You shall not be a familiar to humans like the Servants.
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の使い魔に甘んじる事もなくなる
findings.governingReading: Saber would no longer have to resign herself to being a human’s familiar as Servants do.
findings.explanation: The English removes 甘んじる, the humiliating acquiescence to a lower status central to Archer’s temptation.

findings.highlight: She must have realized that fighting is the only way.
findings.evidenceJa: もはや戦うだけと踏み切ったのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps Saber has now committed herself to fighting as the only remaining course.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s reading of Saber’s decision into certainty and turns decisive commitment into realization.

findings.highlight: I have obtained everything
findings.evidenceJa: この世の財は全て手に入れた
findings.governingReading: He has already obtained all the wealth or treasures of this world.
findings.explanation: Everything universalizes a claim specifically about worldly wealth and possessions.

findings.highlight: Saber’s presence freezes
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの気迫が凍り付く
findings.governingReading: Saber’s fighting spirit or force of will freezes.
findings.explanation: Presence changes an internal martial intensity into an external aura or location-like quality.

findings.highlight: others using what is mine
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の物を他人に使われる
findings.governingReading: having his property used by another person
findings.explanation: The later English “strangers” narrows 他人 from anyone other than the owner to unfamiliar people.

findings.highlight: Saber’s body grows misty
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの体が霞む
findings.governingReading: Saber’s body blurs from view.
findings.explanation: Misty implies vaporous transformation where the source describes visual blurring during instant armor manifestation.

findings.highlight: slashes her invisible sword
findings.evidenceJa: 不可視の剣を叩き込む
findings.governingReading: drives or slams the invisible sword into him
findings.explanation: Slashes changes a forceful committed impact into a cutting motion.

findings.highlight: In the short battle
findings.evidenceJa: 一瞬の攻防の合間に
findings.governingReading: within the instant of attack and defense
findings.explanation: Short battle expands one instantaneous exchange into a battle and blurs the enemy’s impossible arming speed.

findings.highlight: running up to the golden  knight,  knight without hesitation
findings.evidenceJa: 黄金の騎士へ跳びこんだ
findings.governingReading: Saber leaps at the golden knight.
findings.explanation: The active English retains two colliding noun-phrase revisions and adds “without hesitation” without source support.

findings.highlight: Combinations like a strobe.
findings.evidenceJa: 閃光装置を見るかのような連撃
findings.governingReading: a succession of blows like watching a strobe or flash device
findings.explanation: Combinations is the wrong combat noun and the fragment does not express the rapid succession of attacks.

findings.highlight: drives magical energy into her sword
findings.evidenceJa: 有り余る魔力を剣に載せ
findings.governingReading: loads her sword with her overflowing surplus of magical power
findings.explanation: The English removes the excessive abundance that powers Saber’s lightning-like barrage.

findings.highlight: The man hasn’t even drawn his weapon yet.
findings.evidenceJa: 男は帯剣していない
findings.governingReading: The man is not carrying or wearing a sword.
findings.explanation: Not drawn implies a present sheathed weapon; the source says he is not bearing a sword at all.

findings.highlight: he is just protecting his head with his hands
findings.evidenceJa: 両手でかろうじて頭を守っているだけ
findings.governingReading: all he can do is barely protect his head with both hands
findings.explanation: The English drops both arms and the fact that his defense only barely succeeds.

findings.highlight: And on top of that, Saber’s sword is invisible.
findings.evidenceJa: 加えて、セイバーの剣は不可視だ
findings.governingReading: Japanese page51 continues the sword analysis; its English counterpart should occupy the same label.
findings.explanation: The comparator has no page51 and instead labels this passage as the first of two page53 occurrences, breaking label-level alignment.

findings.highlight: keeps hitting the man’s armor
findings.evidenceJa: 面白いように、男の鎧に直撃する
findings.governingReading: strikes the man’s armor with almost absurd or gratifying ease
findings.explanation: The English omits the narrator’s evaluation of how readily every invisible blow lands.

findings.highlight: one-sided elimination
findings.evidenceJa: 一方的な殲滅戦
findings.governingReading: a one-sided war of annihilation
findings.explanation: Elimination is an awkward result noun and removes the scale and combat framing of 戦.

findings.highlight: You certainly do have a large supply of magical energy.
findings.evidenceJa: 相変わらず底なしの魔力
findings.governingReading: Saber’s magical power remains as bottomless as ever.
findings.explanation: Large supply weakens the enemy’s claim from effectively unfathomable reserves to ordinary abundance.

findings.highlight: My armor does not give out often
findings.evidenceJa: 我の鎧が軋みをあげるなど、そうあり得る事ではない
findings.governingReading: It is exceedingly rare for his armor even to creak under strain.
findings.explanation: Giving out changes the armor’s first audible strain into outright failure and alters the threshold of Saber’s achievement.

findings.highlight: raises his hand to the night sky
findings.evidenceJa: 何もない、ただ夜が広がるだけの空間に腕を伸ばし
findings.governingReading: extends his arm into empty space where only the night spreads
findings.explanation: Night sky relocates the gesture upward and removes the anomalous emptiness into which the weapon appears.

findings.highlight: Saber attacks with all her power.
findings.evidenceJa: 一際大きく構えをとり、セイバーは渾身の一撃を放つ
findings.governingReading: Saber takes an exceptionally broad stance and unleashes a full-body, all-out blow.
findings.explanation: The English retains power but omits the enlarged stance that physically telegraphs the decisive strike.

findings.highlight: curse of [r]vengeance
findings.evidenceJa: 復讐の呪詛
findings.governingReading: a Noble Phantasm bearing a curse of vengeance
findings.explanation: A raw [r] control tag splits the English word “vengeance” inside Saber’s spoken line.

findings.highlight: Saber distances herself
findings.evidenceJa: 二度間合いを離し
findings.governingReading: Saber disengages and opens the interval for a second time.
findings.explanation: The English removes that this is Saber’s second deliberate separation, weakening the developing tactical pattern.

findings.highlight: it means that the enemy’s attacks are revealed
findings.evidenceJa: 同時に手の内が見えた
findings.governingReading: at the same time, the enemy has shown part of his hand or means
findings.explanation: The English overstates one visible weapon into revelation of the enemy’s attacks as a class.

findings.highlight: his armor is at its limit
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツの鎧も限界が近い
findings.governingReading: his armor is nearing its limit
findings.explanation: The English promotes proximity to the limit into arrival at it.

findings.highlight: Gate of Babylon.
findings.evidenceJa: “王の財宝”
findings.governingReading: “The King’s Treasury,” read as Gate of Babylon
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby reading and removes the written Noble Phantasm name that identifies the revealed function as the king’s treasury.

findings.highlight: Saber’s body stops.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの体がズレる
findings.governingReading: Saber’s body slips or is displaced off line.
findings.explanation: Stops replaces lateral displacement under the unexpected weapon exchange with cessation of movement.

findings.highlight: Saber retreats, covered in ice.
findings.evidenceJa: 氷に覆われながらも咄嗟に後退する
findings.governingReading: Even while ice covers her, Saber retreats instantly on reflex.
findings.explanation: The English omits the concessive resistance and split-second response.

findings.highlight: a sickle-like weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 死神の鎌めいた凶器
findings.governingReading: a lethal weapon resembling the Grim Reaper’s scythe
findings.explanation: Sickle-like removes the death-personification image and weakens 凶器 into a neutral weapon.

findings.highlight: The sickle goes through her arm like the gauntlet isn’t there
findings.evidenceJa: 鎌はセイバーの籠手などないように貫通し
findings.governingReading: The scythe passes through as though Saber’s gauntlet did not exist.
findings.explanation: The English invents physical penetration through Saber’s arm; the source describes bypassing the gauntlet before stealing magical power.

findings.highlight: As if cutting away her bone
findings.evidenceJa: 骨そのものを抜き取るかのように
findings.governingReading: as though pulling the bone itself out of the targeted place
findings.explanation: Cutting changes an extraction simile into severing and makes the imagined bodily mechanism more literal.

findings.highlight: drawing magical energy into her arm
findings.evidenceJa: 麻痺した片腕に魔力を通しながら
findings.governingReading: channeling magical power through her one paralyzed arm
findings.explanation: The English omits both paralysis and that only one arm is affected.

findings.highlight: Many handles
findings.evidenceJa: 無数の柄
findings.governingReading: countless weapon hilts
findings.explanation: Many reduces the explicitly innumerable scale that motivates Saber’s impossible-Noble-Phantasm reaction.

findings.highlight: I can feel that they are infinite.
findings.evidenceJa: その数はそれこそ底なしなのだと実感できる
findings.governingReading: Though unseen, their number feels bottomless to Shirou.
findings.explanation: Infinite promotes a sensory impression and metaphor into an exact categorical quantity.

findings.highlight: all the divine mysteries from every legend
findings.evidenceJa: ありとあらゆる伝承に潜む神秘の全て
findings.governingReading: every mystery hidden within traditions of every age and place
findings.explanation: Divine adds godhood to 神秘 and removes the sense that these mysteries lie concealed within the traditions.

findings.highlight: A Servant will not answer when asked their true identity.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントが真名を問われ
findings.governingReading: when a Servant is asked for their True Name
findings.explanation: Identity broadens the formal system term and weakens the taboo governing Servant disclosure.

findings.highlight: he has to be Cu Chulainn
findings.evidenceJa: 槍の持ち主
findings.governingReading: he would have to be the spear’s owner, read as Cu Chulainn
findings.explanation: The English retains only the ruby identification and removes Shirou’s surface reasoning from possession to owner.

findings.highlight: if it was a fake
findings.evidenceJa: あの宝具が全て偽物であったのなら
findings.governingReading: if all of those Noble Phantasms were counterfeits
findings.explanation: The English changes the entire arsenal being false into one unspecified object being fake.

findings.highlight: the model of weapon
findings.evidenceJa: 原型の、武器
findings.governingReading: prototype weapons
findings.explanation: Model of weapon is malformed and can imply a representation; Shirou realizes “original” may mean archetypal prototypes.

findings.highlight: only those that originate in that land
findings.evidenceJa: その土地に帰順した物だけ
findings.governingReading: only traditions that submitted or became assimilated to that land
findings.explanation: Originate reverses the relation: the source describes traditions adapted to a land, not necessarily born there.

findings.highlight: a form before they were given names
findings.evidenceJa: そう呼ばれる前のカタチ
findings.governingReading: a form that existed before such things came to be called Noble Phantasms
findings.explanation: Given names makes the issue personal naming, while Shirou is reasoning about the category and historical form before the designation “Noble Phantasm.”

findings.highlight: My body has only recovered to the point where I can barely move my fingers.
findings.evidenceJa: 手足。体はようやく、歯を食いしばって指が動く程度
findings.governingReading: His limbs remain disabled; even clenching his teeth, his body has recovered only enough to move his fingers.
findings.explanation: The English omits the limb inventory and the clenched effort required for even finger movement.

findings.highlight: They were valued because they were splendid swords
findings.evidenceJa: 名剣であるが故に重宝され活躍し
findings.governingReading: Because they were celebrated blades, they were prized and saw active use.
findings.explanation: The English omits the weapons’ subsequent deeds, the step by which scattered treasury objects become later Noble Phantasms.

findings.highlight: every legend, myth, folklore, and Noble Phantasm
findings.evidenceJa: 各国に伝わる神話、伝承、宝具
findings.governingReading: the myths, traditions, and Noble Phantasms passed down in every country
findings.explanation: The English splits 伝承 into both legend and folklore, inventing a fourth category and blurring the three-part list.

findings.highlight: a “model” must exist
findings.evidenceJa: 必ず“原型”は存在する
findings.governingReading: a prototype or original form must exist
findings.explanation: Model suggests an exemplar used for imitation; Shirou is tracing later weapons backward to an originating prototype.

findings.highlight: One said to rule over ancient Mesopotamia.
findings.evidenceJa: 古代メソポタミアに君臨したという魔人
findings.governingReading: the supernatural or demonic figure said to have reigned in ancient Mesopotamia
findings.explanation: The English omits 魔人, removing a key characterization immediately before the half-divine king’s identification.

findings.highlight: accepts the shock with satisfaction
findings.evidenceJa: その響きを満足げに受け止める
findings.governingReading: Gilgamesh receives the sound or resonance of his name with satisfaction.
findings.explanation: The English makes Saber’s shock the object of his satisfaction instead of the spoken resonance of “Gilgamesh.”

findings.highlight: his many Noble Phantasms
findings.evidenceJa: 有り余る宝具
findings.governingReading: his superabundant, inexhaustible supply of Noble Phantasms
findings.explanation: Many removes the sense of surplus abundance established by the bottomless treasury.

findings.highlight: defeat his enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵を粉砕する
findings.governingReading: pulverize or crush the enemy
findings.explanation: Defeat neutralizes the violent totality of Gilgamesh’s intended finishing action.

findings.highlight: He too must know the holy sword’s power
findings.evidenceJa: 聖剣の力は知っているのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps he too knows the power of Saber’s holy sword.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s reading of Gilgamesh’s visible loss of composure into certainty.

findings.highlight: It must have been when she attacked him earlier.
findings.evidenceJa: 先ほどの剣戟の間だろう
findings.governingReading: It was probably during the preceding sword exchange.
findings.explanation: Must overstates Shirou’s reconstruction, and attacked him narrows the reciprocal sword-clash interval.

findings.highlight: The pain is telling me I will break if I move any further.
findings.evidenceJa: 体中にはしった罅が、これ以上動けば砕けてしまう
findings.governingReading: The cracks running throughout his body warn that they will shatter if he moves farther.
findings.explanation: The English replaces concrete cracks and their impending propagation with a generalized personified pain.

findings.highlight: I bear my pain.
findings.evidenceJa: 痛みをかみ殺す
findings.governingReading: He bites back or suppresses the pain.
findings.explanation: Bear describes endurance but loses the active effort to prevent pain from showing or interrupting him.

findings.highlight: I have a bad feeling about this.
findings.evidenceJa: 悪寒がする
findings.governingReading: A physical chill runs through him.
findings.explanation: Bad feeling turns a bodily symptom of dread into generic intuition, flattening the link between injury, fear, and foreboding.

findings.highlight: A holy sword
findings.evidenceJa: 音に聞こえし聖剣
findings.governingReading: the famed holy sword known by reputation
findings.explanation: The English omits Gilgamesh’s acknowledgment of Excalibur’s renown.

findings.highlight: the golden knight does not back away
findings.evidenceJa: 黄金の騎士は怯まない
findings.governingReading: the golden knight does not flinch
findings.explanation: Back away changes an involuntary failure of nerve into physical retreat.

findings.highlight: a rock drill to pierce through a hard surface
findings.evidenceJa: 固い岩盤を貫いていく削岩機
findings.governingReading: a rock drill boring through solid bedrock
findings.explanation: Hard surface removes the geological mass and resistance that make Ea’s rotating blade physically uncanny.

findings.highlight: I have always wanted to take the sword
findings.evidenceJa: その剣、一度味わってみたくもあった
findings.governingReading: He has wanted to taste or experience that strongest sword once.
findings.explanation: Take the sword can mean seize possession and adds “always”; the source expresses a desire to experience its attack once.

findings.highlight: His laughter echoes through the park.
findings.evidenceJa: 押し殺した笑いが響く
findings.governingReading: A suppressed laugh sounds out.
findings.explanation: The English omits suppression and invents the park as the space through which the laugh echoes.

findings.highlight: She must consider that provocation.
findings.evidenceJa: 挑発と受け止めたのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps Saber takes it as a provocation.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s question about Saber’s response into certainty and is grammatically awkward.

findings.highlight: try to defend yourself against my sword
findings.evidenceJa: 我が剣、見事受けきってみるがいい
findings.governingReading: Try to withstand my sword completely and magnificently.
findings.explanation: Defend yourself generalizes Saber’s challenge to receive the full attack without failing.

findings.highlight: The Noble Phantasm released with its true name
findings.evidenceJa: 所有者によって名を解放された宝具
findings.governingReading: The Noble Phantasm whose name is released by its owner
findings.explanation: The English removes the owner as actor and changes release of the name into release of the weapon by means of a name.

findings.highlight: EX
findings.evidenceJa: 約束された
findings.governingReading: “Promised,” read as the first half of Excalibur
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the phonetic ruby and removes the first half of the written title “The Sword of Promised Victory.”

findings.highlight: CALIBUR
findings.evidenceJa: 勝利の剣
findings.governingReading: “Sword of Victory,” read as the second half of Excalibur
findings.explanation: The English removes the completion of the written Noble Phantasm title.

findings.highlight: releases the holy sword
findings.evidenceJa: 気合いと共に解放する
findings.governingReading: releases the holy sword together with a forceful battle cry or focused shout
findings.explanation: The English omits Saber’s vocalized exertion at the instant of release.

findings.highlight: Enuma Elish
findings.evidenceJa: 天地乖離す、開闢の星
findings.governingReading: “The Star of Creation that Split Heaven and Earth,” read as Enuma Elish
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the ruby and removes the full written Noble Phantasm title.

findings.highlight: A light of the same magnitude
findings.evidenceJa: まったく同位の光
findings.governingReading: a light of precisely the same rank or level
findings.explanation: Magnitude reduces a qualitative parity of standing to quantitative brightness or size.

findings.highlight: A huge  impact.  impact[line2]!!
findings.evidenceJa: 凄まじいまでの衝突
findings.governingReading: an impact of staggering violence
findings.explanation: The active English contains two colliding punctuated versions of “impact.”

findings.highlight: burning my  eyes.  eyes…!
findings.evidenceJa: 目蓋を焼く
findings.governingReading: burning his eyelids
findings.explanation: The English changes eyelids to eyes and retains two competing punctuation variants.

findings.highlight: dig myself into the ground
findings.evidenceJa: 地面にへばりつきながら
findings.governingReading: clings desperately to the ground with one arm
findings.explanation: Dig invents penetration into the earth and loses the flattened clinging posture.

findings.highlight: battle of the two rumblings
findings.evidenceJa: 拮抗した両者の奔流
findings.governingReading: the two opposing torrents locked in equilibrium
findings.explanation: Rumblings replaces flows of power and the English phrase is malformed, obscuring the apparent stalemate before reversal.

findings.highlight: my blinded eyes
findings.evidenceJa: 光で鈍った目
findings.governingReading: eyes dulled or impaired by the light
findings.explanation: Blinded overstates temporary visual impairment into loss of sight.

findings.highlight: I thought she might be dead.
findings.evidenceJa: 死んでいる、と思った
findings.governingReading: Shirou thought she was dead.
findings.explanation: Might weakens the immediate, definite impression that the next sentence explicitly attributes to Saber’s mutilated appearance.

findings.highlight: the most powerful holy sword
findings.evidenceJa: 人類最強の聖剣
findings.governingReading: humanity’s strongest holy sword
findings.explanation: The English omits humanity as the comparison class in Gilgamesh’s taunt.
